candidates.rationale: Fusion: A prices balance-sheet deterioration but conditions it on liquidity (volume-vs-range corr); B is pure price geometry with no fundamental. The child conditions the leverage penalty on whether the market has already marked the name down: the 5-day floor relative to the quarterly floor says how far above its own low the name still sits, so levering-up names trading well above their quarterly low have the repricing ahead of them, while ones already at the floor have it priced. That is a conditioning variable neither parent has (A conditions on trading activity, B on nothing). Donations: TS_DELTA($leverage, 63) from A (3 nodes), TS_MIN($low, 5) from B (3 nodes). Wrappers chosen to dodge the archive: CS_ZSCORE(TS_DELTA($leverage,63)), CS_RANK(MAX(...,0)), CS_RANK(ABS(...)) and CS_RANK(-...) are all 4-node archive blocks, CS_DEMEAN is not; B's 7-node true-range denominator TS_MAX($high,5)-TS_MIN($low,5) is itself an archive subtree so only the floor leg is taken. A's CS_DEMEAN(CS_RANK($roe)) prefix is deliberately not donated: it appears in five archive members and dominates rank correlation. Limits: 2 fields, 0 free constants, depth 5, 88 chars.

Bad cross, stated rather than forced. B is a 9-node tree whose complete subtrees are $volume (1), $high - $low (3), TS_DELTA($high - $low, 5) (5) and the TS_CORR (8). Everything at 4 nodes or more is a subtree of B itself, which is in the archive, so the only legal donation from B is $high - $low, and A contains that same block: there is no pair of distinct donations, hence no genuine fusion. The volume-vs-range correlation kernel is also saturated (six archive members; a $volume-for-$dollar_volume swap on it drew a rho 0.990 reject), so B's actual content cannot be reused at all. Nearest legal factor returned: A donates TS_MIN($low, 5) (3 nodes) as the floor of the trading envelope, B donates $high - $low (3 nodes), and the numerator carries B's range-change idea stripped of its volume leg as the 10-day dispersion of the daily range, normalised by the envelope so it is unit-free. Windows chosen off the archive: TS_STD($high - $low, 21) and TS_MAX($high,21)-TS_MIN($low,21) are existing blocks, 10 and the mixed 21/5 envelope are not. Expect a weak price-only factor (price-only accepts in this archive score 0.08-0.72).

Fusion: B is DuPont operating quality (margin times turnover, financing stripped out) with no timing at all; A is an intraday-range signal with no fundamental. The child uses range expansion, fast range over slow range, as the timing gate on the quality sort: an operationally efficient name is only worth holding while the market is actively repricing it, and range expansion dates that repricing. Neither parent has the interaction - B fires every day regardless of what price is doing, A has no cross-section of firm quality. Donations: $operating_margin * $asset_turnover from B (3 nodes), $high - $low from A (3 nodes; A's only legal block, since TS_DELTA($high - $low, 5) at 5 nodes and the TS_CORR at 8 nodes are both subtrees of the archived A). CS_ZSCORE rather than CS_RANK on the fundamental because CS_RANK($operating_margin * $asset_turnover) is exactly B, a 4-node archive block. Range windows 5 and 42 are free; TS_MEAN($high - $low, w) already exists at w = 10, 21 and 63, and TS_SUM($high - $low, 5) is an archive block. Limits: 4 fields, 0 free constants, depth 6, 119 chars.

Fusion: quality times price impact. B asks whether volume co-moves with the daily range; the child replaces that correlation with its level form, range per unit of share volume, an Amihud-style impact proxy. Crossed with A's DuPont quality the factor says quality is left underpriced where arbitrage is expensive to run, so the payoff to operating efficiency is concentrated in the high-impact half of the cross-section. A alone is a static quality tilt with no state variable; B alone is a liquidity sort with no cross-section of firm quality. Donations: $operating_margin * $asset_turnover from A (3 nodes), $high - $low from B (3 nodes; B's only legal block, its 6-node TS_CORR being the archive member itself). Wrapper is CS_DEMEAN because CS_RANK($operating_margin * $asset_turnover) is A itself and CS_ZSCORE of it is claimed by the pair-3 child. Denominator uses $volume, not $dollar_volume: ($high - $low) / ($dollar_volume + 1e-8) is a 5-node archive block. Limits: 5 fields (at the cap), 0 free constants, depth 4, 91 chars.

Fusion: the direction of the balance-sheet move flips the sign of the range signal. Range volatility on its own is a two-sided statistic - A cannot tell distress from a washout - and B's leverage terms are a static tilt that never says when the balance sheet is being priced. The child makes the leverage delta a regime switch: a name levering up while its daily range destabilises is having credit risk impounded and keeps going, a name deleveraging into the same instability is a forced-seller washout that reverts. That sign-flip conditioner exists in neither parent. Donations: $high - $low from A (3 nodes, A's only legal block), TS_DELTA($leverage, 63) from B (3 nodes; B's CS_RANK($roe) - CS_RANK($leverage) is a 5-node and CS_RANK(TS_DELTA($leverage, 63)) a 4-node subtree of the archived B). SIGN is the only wrapper on that delta not already an archive block (CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE, ABS, MAX and unary minus are all taken). $roe is dropped on purpose: eleven archive members carry it and it dominates rank correlation. TS_STD($high - $low, 42) is free; window 21 is taken. Limits: 3 fields, 0 free constants, depth 4, 65 chars.

Fusion: leverage growth read through jump concentration. B amplifies its accrual/quality spread by a smooth 42-day correlation of range with dollar volume, an attention measure that cannot distinguish news from drift; A penalises leverage growth with no state variable at all. The child conditions on the share of a quarter's total trading range delivered on its single widest day, so the leverage delta only fires where the repricing arrives in discrete credit news rather than as continuous churn. Neither parent has that shape measure. Donations: TS_DELTA($leverage, 63) from A (3 nodes; A's rank spread CS_RANK($roe) - CS_RANK($leverage) and CS_RANK(TS_DELTA($leverage, 63)) are 5- and 4-node archive blocks), $high - $low from B (3 nodes; B's own spread and its TS_CORR are 5- and 6-node archive blocks). One outer CS_RANK keeps the raw delta's scale out of the product. TS_MAX($high - $low, 21) and TS_SUM($high - $low, 63) are both free; TS_SUM($high - $low, 5) is an archive block. Limits: 3 fields, 0 free constants, depth 5, 96 chars.

Fusion: accrual reversal conditioned on the gap share of risk. B's vol term structure is return-only, so it cannot say where the volatility comes from; A's attention leg is a range-versus-dollar-volume correlation. The child keeps B's short leg and re-bases it on A's intraday range: five-day close-to-close volatility measured against the range actually traded through over the month is the fraction of risk arriving outside the session, i.e. overnight news rather than intraday churn. Accrual-inflated earnings are corrected on news, so the reversal is collected where that share is high - a conditioner neither parent has. Donations: TS_STD($return, 5) from B (3 nodes; its guarded 63-day leg is a 5-node and the full ratio a 9-node subtree of the archived B), $high - $low from A (3 nodes, A's only legal block). TS_SUM($high - $low, 21) is free, while TS_MEAN($high - $low, 21) + 1e-8 and TS_MEAN($high - $low, 63) + 1e-8 are archive blocks. Note the residual correlation risk against the archived CS_ZSCORE($accrual_gap) * CS_RANK(TS_STD($high - $low, 21) / (TS_MEAN($high - $low, 63) + 1e-8)): same fundamental leg, but the price leg here is a cross-scale gap share rather than a range-on-range dispersion. Limits: 4 fields, 0 free constants, depth 6, 87 chars.

Bad cross, stated rather than forced. A is five nodes in total (the difference, two CS_RANKs, $roe, $volume); its only complete subtree of three or more nodes is the whole expression, which is the archive member itself. So the two rules collide: any child that mechanically keeps 3 nodes of A necessarily shares 5 nodes with an archive member and is rejected before scoring. No compliant crossover with this parent exists. Nearest legal factor returned: B donates TS_STD($return, 5) (3 nodes; its guarded 63-day leg is a 5-node archive subtree of B, so the short leg is the only one that can be taken), and A's economic content is rebuilt rather than copied. Turnover divided by the volatility that would justify it is churn not explained by news - disagreement and noise trading - and quality is underpriced where that churn is highest, which turns A's two independent additive sorts into an interaction. A field swap on A's spread would not have worked either: $roa for $roe on the same spread has measured at rho 0.859 against the parent. Limits: 3 fields, 0 free constants, depth 5, 62 chars.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: CROSSOVER. Each pair below holds two parents from DIFFERENT archive
niches. Return one child per pair that genuinely combines them.

A child must keep a complete sub-expression of at least 3 nodes
from EACH parent, checked mechanically; a child that is really just one parent
with cosmetic changes is rejected. Put both parent ids in `parent_ids`.

In the rationale, state the fusion logic: what does the combination capture that
neither parent captures alone? A conditioning variable, a normaliser, an
interaction. If you cannot name one, the pair is a bad cross and you should say
so in the rationale rather than force it.

  B [4d336036d396e2d9]  CS_ZSCORE(TS_SUM($high - $low, 5) / (TS_MAX($high, 5) - TS_MIN($low, 5) + 1e-8))
